set: Certified Information Security Manager (CISM) practice – 2026 Governance and Security Management

questions.stem: An organization has approved a three-year business strategy that includes entering new markets and expanding its digital services. The information security manager has been asked to update the information security strategy. Which of the following should be the FIRST consideration?
options: The capabilities of the organization's existing security technologies
The business objectives, risk appetite, and requirements of the expansion
The availability of qualified personnel to operate additional controls
The security frameworks adopted by competitors in the new markets
questions.explanation: An information security strategy must support enterprise objectives while remaining consistent with the organization's risk appetite and obligations. Understanding the business direction establishes the basis for security priorities, investments, and capabilities. Existing technologies, staffing, and industry practices are relevant considerations after the strategic requirements have been identified.
questions.source: ISACA CISM Exam Content Outline, Domain 1: Information Security Strategy

questions.stem: An organization is establishing an enterprise-wide information security governance framework. Which of the following parties should have ultimate oversight responsibility for the organization's information security governance?
options: The information security operations team
The internal audit department
The information technology steering committee
The board of directors or designated governing body
questions.explanation: Ultimate oversight of information security governance rests with the board or an appropriately designated governing body. This body ensures that security supports enterprise objectives and that management is accountable for managing information security risk. Security teams implement the program, while internal audit provides independent assurance.
questions.source: ISACA CISM Exam Content Outline, Domain 1: Enterprise Governance

questions.stem: A multinational organization is consolidating several independently developed digital platforms into a common enterprise architecture. Each business unit uses different authentication mechanisms, data classifications, and network trust models. The information security manager has been asked to develop an information security architecture that supports the consolidation while minimizing disruption. Which of the following is the BEST approach?
options: Define common security architecture principles based on business risk and integrate them into enterprise architecture decisions
Adopt the security architecture of the business unit that has experienced the fewest reported security incidents
Require all business units to retain their existing controls until the technology consolidation has been completed
Select a standardized security technology platform before evaluating the dependencies between business services
questions.explanation: Information security architecture should translate business risk requirements into consistent security principles and capabilities within the enterprise architecture. This approach allows the organization to address shared dependencies, trust boundaries, and control requirements while accommodating justified business differences. Historical incident counts or premature technology standardization do not establish whether an architecture appropriately addresses enterprise risk.
questions.subtopic: Enterprise Architecture and Security Strategy Alignment
questions.source: ISACA, CISM Exam Content Update, September 2026: Enterprise Architecture

questions.stem: An information security manager is preparing a business case for an identity management initiative. Senior management has indicated that funding is limited and that several business projects are competing for the same resources. Which of the following would BEST support approval of the security initiative?
options: A comparison of the technical capabilities offered by competing identity management products
A report showing how many organizations in the same industry have implemented similar systems
An assessment of expected risk reduction, business benefits, implementation costs, and available alternatives
A detailed implementation schedule demonstrating that the initiative can be completed within the financial year
questions.explanation: A compelling security business case connects the proposed investment to business objectives and demonstrates its expected value relative to costs and alternatives. Quantifying or otherwise substantiating risk reduction helps management compare the initiative with competing uses of resources. Technical features, industry adoption, and delivery schedules alone do not establish business justification.
questions.subtopic: Strategic Planning and Business Case Development
questions.source: ISACA CISM Exam Content Outline, Domain 1: Strategic Planning

questions.stem: A financial services organization has implemented additional controls to reduce the likelihood and impact of unauthorized access to customer records. The information security manager is evaluating the level of exposure that remains after these controls have been applied. Which of the following BEST describes this exposure?
options: Inherent risk
Residual risk
Control risk
Emerging risk
questions.explanation: Residual risk is the risk remaining after management has implemented risk responses, including security controls. It must be evaluated against the organization's risk appetite and applicable risk tolerance limits. Inherent risk represents exposure before considering the effects of controls.
questions.source: ISACA CISM Exam Content Outline, Domain 2: Information Security Risk Assessment

questions.stem: A risk assessment identifies that a legacy application exposes sensitive information to unauthorized access. The proposed remediation is costly, and the business unit wishes to continue operating the application without additional controls. The remaining risk exceeds the organization's established tolerance. What should the information security manager do NEXT?
options: Document the business unit's decision and close the risk assessment
Implement additional controls without consulting the business unit
Transfer responsibility for the risk decision to the internal audit function
Escalate the exposure to the appropriate risk authority for a decision consistent with governance requirements
questions.explanation: A business unit's willingness to accept exposure does not automatically authorize acceptance of risk exceeding established tolerance. The information security manager should communicate the exposure and available responses to the authority responsible for such decisions under the governance framework. Any exception or change in risk appetite must follow the organization's approved authorization and escalation processes.
questions.source: ISACA CISM Exam Content Outline, Domain 2: Information Security Risk Response

questions.stem: An organization is migrating several revenue-critical services to a cloud provider that has strong security certifications and favorable independent audit reports. During the assessment, the information security manager discovers that the provider relies on one regional infrastructure dependency for multiple services. An extended outage of this dependency could interrupt several business functions simultaneously. Which of the following should be the PRIMARY consideration in determining the appropriate risk response?
options: The aggregated business impact of the shared dependency and the effectiveness of available continuity measures
The provider's compliance certifications and the frequency of its independent security assessments
The estimated cost of purchasing additional cybersecurity insurance for the affected business services
The number of technical vulnerabilities identified during the provider's most recent penetration test
questions.explanation: Shared infrastructure dependencies can create concentration risk that is not adequately represented by individual service assessments or security certifications. The manager should evaluate the combined business impact, recovery requirements, and effectiveness of potential risk treatments before recommending a response. Technical assurance and insurance may inform the decision but cannot substitute for understanding the organization's exposure to a common failure.
questions.subtopic: Third-Party Concentration Risk and Risk Assessment
questions.source: ISACA CISM Exam Content Outline, Domain 2: Risk Assessment and Risk Response

questions.stem: An organization's key risk indicator for privileged access exceptions has exceeded its approved threshold for three consecutive reporting periods. Existing security controls remain operational, and no related breach has been detected. Which of the following is the BEST action for the information security manager?
options: Continue monitoring until an incident demonstrates that the existing controls are ineffective
Increase the reporting frequency without changing the underlying risk assessment
Investigate the trend, reassess the associated risk, and report the results to the appropriate risk owners
Immediately replace the privileged access management system with a more restrictive technical solution
questions.explanation: An established risk threshold being exceeded is a signal that the organization's exposure or control effectiveness may have changed. The manager should investigate the underlying causes, reassess the risk, and communicate material findings to the responsible decision-makers. A confirmed security incident is not required before risk management action becomes appropriate.
questions.source: ISACA CISM Exam Content Outline, Domain 2: Risk Monitoring and Reporting

questions.stem: An organization is implementing an information classification scheme to protect sensitive business information. Who should be primarily responsible for determining the classification of a particular business information asset?
options: The system administrator responsible for storing the information
The designated business information owner
The information security analyst responsible for monitoring access
The internal auditor responsible for reviewing information controls
questions.explanation: The designated business information owner is accountable for determining classification based on the information's sensitivity, value, and business requirements. Information security personnel can establish classification standards and advise owners, while administrators implement the corresponding controls. Classification decisions should reflect business accountability rather than technical custody.
questions.source: ISACA CISM Exam Content Outline, Domain 3: Information Asset Identification and Classification

questions.stem: A company is developing a customer-facing digital platform that will integrate internal systems, external application programming interfaces, and cloud services. The information security manager wants to avoid expensive security redesign after implementation. Which of the following would be the BEST approach?
options: Schedule a comprehensive penetration test immediately before production deployment
Require each development team to select security controls independently for its components
Base the security design primarily on the default controls provided by the cloud service vendors
Integrate security requirements and architecture reviews into the platform's initial design and development processes
questions.explanation: Integrating security requirements into architecture and development decisions allows threats, dependencies, and trust boundaries to be addressed before design choices become difficult to change. Security architecture should support business requirements while establishing consistent protection across internal and external components. Late testing remains valuable but is less effective at preventing fundamental architectural weaknesses.
questions.subtopic: Information Security Architecture and Secure Development
questions.source: ISACA, CISM Exam Content Update, September 2026: Information Security Architecture

questions.stem: An organization's security program reports that 98% of required controls passed their most recent compliance tests. Nevertheless, significant security incidents involving previously identified risk scenarios continue to occur. Senior management asks whether the existing program is providing adequate protection. Which of the following is the BEST approach for the information security manager?
options: Assess whether control design and operating effectiveness adequately address the current risk scenarios and desired business outcomes
Increase the number of compliance tests performed each quarter to improve the confidence level of the reported results
Replace controls associated with recent incidents regardless of their documented purpose or existing effectiveness
Recalculate the overall compliance score using greater weight for controls associated with critical business systems
questions.explanation: Passing compliance tests does not necessarily demonstrate that a control is suitable for the threats and business risks it is intended to address. The manager should examine both control design and operating effectiveness, including whether the controls produce the required risk reduction. This distinguishes compliance with specified requirements from the overall effectiveness of the security program.
questions.subtopic: Information Security Control Testing and Evaluation
questions.source: ISACA CISM Exam Content Outline, Domain 3: Security Control Design, Testing and Evaluation

questions.stem: An organization uses an external service provider to process confidential customer information. The provider proposes engaging a subcontractor to host the information in a new environment. Before approving the arrangement, which of the following is the BEST action for the information security manager?
options: Request a written statement from the primary provider confirming that its security controls remain unchanged
Require the subcontractor to implement exactly the same security technologies used by the organization
Evaluate the subcontractor-related risks and ensure appropriate security and oversight obligations extend to the subcontractor
Transfer responsibility for assessing the subcontractor's security posture entirely to the primary service provider
questions.explanation: Using subcontractors introduces additional dependencies and risks that must be considered in the organization's third-party risk management process. The manager should ensure that the assessment and contractual arrangements address the subcontractor's access, controls, incident obligations, and monitoring requirements. Outsourcing service delivery does not eliminate the organization's accountability for protecting its information.
questions.subtopic: Management of External Services and Fourth Parties
questions.source: ISACA CISM Exam Content Outline, Domain 3: Management of External Services

questions.stem: An organization wants to improve employees' handling of sensitive information through an information security awareness program. Which of the following approaches would BEST support this objective?
options: Provide an identical annual technical security examination to all employees
Deliver role-relevant awareness activities and measure changes in security-related behavior
Distribute the organization's complete security policy library to employees each quarter
Require employees to acknowledge the acceptable use policy after every system login
questions.explanation: Effective security awareness should address the risks employees encounter in their roles and promote observable improvements in behavior. Measuring behavior provides stronger evidence of the program's impact than relying solely on attendance or policy acknowledgment. Training content and reinforcement should be adapted to relevant responsibilities and threats.
questions.source: ISACA CISM Exam Content Outline, Domain 3: Information Security Awareness and Training

questions.stem: Senior management has requested a metric demonstrating whether controls intended to prevent former employees from retaining privileged system access are operating effectively. Which of the following metrics would BEST satisfy this requirement?
options: The total number of privileged accounts maintained across the organization's systems
The number of privileged access reviews performed during the reporting period
The percentage of employees who completed annual access control awareness training
The percentage of terminated employees' privileged accounts disabled within the required timeframe
questions.explanation: The selected metric directly measures whether a control is achieving its defined objective within the organization's required timeframe. It can identify failures in the access termination process and support corrective action. Counts of accounts, reviews, or training completions describe activity but do not directly establish whether former employees' privileged access is promptly removed.
questions.source: ISACA CISM Exam Content Outline, Domain 3: Information Security Program Metrics

questions.stem: An organization is developing recovery priorities for its critical information systems following a major disruption. Which of the following should provide the PRIMARY basis for determining the acceptable duration of business service interruptions?
options: The results of a business impact analysis
The age and configuration of the affected systems
The complexity of the organization's network infrastructure
The recovery capabilities advertised by its technology vendors
questions.explanation: A business impact analysis identifies critical activities, dependencies, and the consequences of disruptions over time. Its findings support business-approved recovery requirements and priorities. Technology limitations influence how recovery objectives can be achieved, but they should not independently determine what disruption the business can tolerate.
questions.source: ISACA CISM Exam Content Outline, Domain 4: Business Impact Analysis

questions.stem: An organization operates an incident response process in which events are classified primarily by the type of malware or attack technique involved. As a result, incidents affecting critical financial services sometimes receive the same response priority as minor events affecting noncritical systems. Which of the following improvements would BEST address this weakness?
options: Increase the number of technical attack categories used by the incident response team
Assign incident priorities according to the time at which security monitoring tools generate alerts
Incorporate business impact, asset criticality, and information sensitivity into incident severity criteria
Allow individual system administrators to determine incident priorities based on their operational workloads
questions.explanation: Incident prioritization should reflect the potential or actual impact on the organization, not simply the technical characteristics of an attack. Business criticality, information sensitivity, and the scope of disruption help determine the urgency of escalation and response. Consistent impact-based classification enables resources to be directed toward the most consequential incidents.
questions.source: ISACA CISM Exam Content Outline, Domain 4: Incident Classification and Categorization

questions.stem: An incident response team has collected system logs and disk images that may be required in a legal investigation. Which of the following practices is MOST important for demonstrating that the evidence has been properly handled?
options: Storing evidence exclusively on the organization's production servers
Documenting evidence collection, custody transfers, and integrity verification
Providing all collected evidence to every member of the incident response team
Deleting duplicate evidence copies immediately after the initial investigation
questions.explanation: A documented chain of custody records who collected, handled, transferred, and controlled evidence throughout its lifecycle. Integrity verification, such as cryptographic hashing where appropriate, helps demonstrate that digital evidence has not been altered. These practices support the reliability and potential admissibility of evidence in legal or regulatory proceedings.
questions.source: ISACA CISM Exam Content Outline, Domain 4: Incident Investigation and Evaluation

questions.stem: An organization has confirmed unauthorized access to a database containing personal information. The investigation is ongoing, and the number of affected records has not yet been established. The organization operates in jurisdictions with different breach notification requirements. What is the BEST approach for the information security manager?
options: Delay all external communications until the forensic investigation has established the complete scope of the incident
Publish an immediate statement confirming that every record in the affected database has been compromised
Delegate all notification decisions to the technical incident response team because it possesses the incident evidence
Coordinate with legal and privacy stakeholders to determine applicable obligations and communicate verified information within required deadlines
questions.explanation: Incident communications must satisfy applicable legal and regulatory requirements while avoiding unsupported statements. The information security manager should coordinate with the relevant legal, privacy, and business stakeholders to establish notification obligations, timing, and approved content. An incomplete investigation does not necessarily justify delaying legally required notifications.
questions.subtopic: Incident Response Communications and Regulatory Notification
questions.source: ISACA CISM Exam Content Outline, Domain 4: Incident Response Communications

questions.stem: A ransomware incident has disrupted an organization's most important customer transaction platform. The incident response team has verified that clean backups are available, but investigation indicates that the attackers may still possess valid privileged credentials. Business management wants the platform restored immediately to limit financial losses. Which of the following is the BEST course of action for the information security manager?
options: Coordinate recovery in an isolated, controlled environment while addressing compromised access and obtaining business authorization for material residual risks
Restore the platform directly to its original production environment because verified backups eliminate the risk of reinfection
Postpone all recovery activities until every affected system has undergone a complete forensic examination and all findings are finalized
Recover the platform using its original privileged accounts and schedule credential replacement after business operations have stabilized
questions.explanation: Recovery must balance business continuity requirements against the risk of further compromise. Isolated recovery, credential containment, and verification of the restored environment can reduce the likelihood of attackers regaining access while supporting timely business restoration. Material residual risks and recovery tradeoffs should be communicated to the appropriate business decision-makers rather than accepted unilaterally by the security team.
questions.source: ISACA CISM Exam Content Outline, Domain 4: Incident Containment and Recovery

questions.stem: Following a major cybersecurity incident, an organization's post-incident review identifies weaknesses in its escalation procedures, monitoring coverage, and coordination between technical and business teams. Which of the following would BEST demonstrate that the organization is using the review to improve incident management capability?
options: Distributing the incident investigation report to all employees without assigning further responsibilities
Increasing the incident response team's budget without identifying which weaknesses require investment
Assigning owners and deadlines to corrective actions and verifying their effectiveness through subsequent testing
Closing the incident after confirming that the affected systems have returned to their normal operating condition
questions.explanation: Post-incident reviews should result in actionable improvements that address identified weaknesses and their underlying causes. Assigning accountability, tracking completion, and validating effectiveness help ensure lessons learned produce measurable changes in preparedness and response. Restoring service or distributing a report alone does not demonstrate that the organization has reduced the likelihood or impact of similar incidents.
questions.source: ISACA CISM Exam Content Outline, Domain 4: Post-Incident Review Practices
